comments.author: Samuel L. Jackson
comments.text: Flight ops has been pushing for this refresh since the last line-check survey flagged attitude tape readability complaints during dawn/dusk approaches. We need the ARINC 661 widget migration and glare work landed and DER-reviewed before the fleet retrofit window opens in Q4.

comments.text: All three epics are past planning and into build. The CGF widget migration team hit a minor snag with vendor toolkit licensing but it's resolved, so I don't expect it to touch our sprint commitment for the symbology refresh.

comments.text: Appreciate the update on the sun-table testing results. The horizon line color compliance issue is the one item I'm watching closely since it's the piece our DER flagged as highest visibility risk during the informal pre-submission review.

The horizon line color palette story remains blocked pending an updated colorimetry reference from the display vendor, and we've escalated that as a dependency risk for next sprint.

epics.title: ARINC 661 Widget Migration for Attitude Tape

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: This epic covers migrating the attitude tape and bank angle pointer off the legacy proprietary symbol set onto ARINC 661 CGF widgets, which is a prerequisite for the DO-178C DAL B recertification package we're assembling for the retrofit customer.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Both attitude tape and bank pointer stories are through peer review now; the main technical risk was primitive-to-widget mapping fidelity, which held up better than expected against our regression baseline.

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Epic is functionally complete — all five leaf items resolved, traceability matrix updated end to end, and the graphics-context leak bug that surfaced mid-month is confirmed fixed under the HIL soak test.

items.title: Re-implement attitude tape as ARINC 661 CGF widget

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Reviewed the CGF widget catalog against the current attitude tape symbol spec — the roll scale and pitch ladder both map cleanly to existing basic widgets, but the sky/ground shading will need a custom composite widget since the vendor toolkit doesn't expose gradient fills natively.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: First working build of the widget-based attitude tape is running on the dev bench; pitch ladder tick spacing matches the legacy rendering within half a pixel across the full +/-90 degree range.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Reviewed the widget composite structure — clean separation of the shading layer from the tick/label layer, just requested a rename on the internal event handler so it doesn't collide with the bank pointer's naming convention.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Deployed to the production CDS build after the flicker fix cleared HIL soak testing overnight with zero anomalies across a simulated 6-hour flight profile.

subtasks.title: Define widget parameter set for attitude tape in CDS

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Drafted the full parameter set — pitch angle, roll angle, slip/skid, and flight director command bars — and mapped each to a CGF widget property with units and update-rate annotations for the requirements traceability matrix.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Parameter set finalized and checked into the ICD; all update rates confirmed against the ARINC 429 label refresh rates coming off the ADIRU.

storyBugs.title: Attitude tape widget flickers during rapid pitch changes

comments.author: Brad Pitt
comments.text: Reproduced a visible one-frame flicker on the sky/ground shading widget during rapid pitch maneuvers above 15 degrees/second on the HIL bench — looks like a double-buffer swap timing issue, not present in the legacy renderer.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Root cause confirmed: the composite widget's shading layer was redrawing on a separate frame callback from the tick/label layer, causing a one-frame tear under high angular rates. Synchronized both layers onto the same widget refresh callback and the flicker is gone in local testing.

comments.author: Brad Pitt
comments.text: Re-ran the full rapid-pitch regression suite on the HIL bench overnight, including the worst-case 25 degrees/second pitch-up scenario, and confirmed zero flicker frames across 40 repetitions.

items.title: Migrate bank angle pointer to ARINC 661 basic widget set

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: The bank pointer is a simpler migration than the attitude tape since it's a single rotating widget, but I flagged a question to the systems team on whether the 45-degree bank alert threshold needs to stay a separate overlay widget or can be baked into the pointer's color state.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Implemented the pointer as a rotating basic widget with color-state driven by the bank alert threshold, which simplified the render tree by removing the old overlay layer entirely.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Peer reviewed — the color-state approach is cleaner than the legacy overlay, no changes requested, just confirmed the alert threshold constant is pulled from the shared config rather than hardcoded.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Resolved and merged into the CDS integration branch; QA confirmed pointer alignment holds within tolerance through the full +/-60 degree roll range on the bench.

subtasks.title: Map legacy bank pointer graphics primitives to CGF widget

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Mapped the legacy triangle-and-arc primitive pair to the CGF rotating pointer widget; the arc scale ticks translate directly to the widget's built-in graduation marks.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Mapping complete and validated pixel-for-pixel against the legacy renderer at 15-degree increments across the full roll range.

storyBugs.title: Bank angle pointer misaligned at extreme roll angles

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: At roll angles beyond 55 degrees the pointer graphic sits roughly 2 degrees off from the commanded value — small, but enough to fail the tolerance spec in the display ICD, and it's consistent and repeatable on the bench.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Found it — the widget's rotation transform was using a small-angle approximation left over from a copy-pasted legacy helper function, which breaks down past 45 degrees. Replaced with the exact trig call and offline validation now matches to within 0.05 degrees at 60 degrees roll.

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: Verified the fix across the full extended roll range up to 75 degrees and it now tracks within spec at every 5-degree increment tested.

items.title: Legacy attitude symbol set leaks graphics context on redraw

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: During an 8-hour soak test of the legacy attitude renderer, memory profiling on the CDS bench showed graphics context handles climbing steadily rather than staying flat, which will eventually starve the display processor on a long-haul flight.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Confirmed the leak — the legacy redraw path allocates a new graphics context handle on every frame instead of reusing the cached one, a holdover from when the renderer supported dynamic resolution switching that we no longer use.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Fix removes the per-frame allocation and reuses a single context handle for the lifetime of the render session; 24-hour soak test on the bench now shows flat handle count.

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: Re-ran the extended 24-hour soak with the fix in place and confirmed zero handle growth, closing this out.

items.title: Update Display Component Requirements Document for CGF widget mapping

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Started updating the DCRD to reflect the new widget-based architecture; the hardest part is re-deriving the traceability links since the old document traced requirements to graphics primitives rather than widget properties.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Reviewed the updated traceability section — recommended splitting the attitude tape requirements into a separate table from the bank pointer ones since the widget mappings are structurally different, which he's incorporating.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: DCRD update complete and submitted to configuration management; every requirement now traces to a specific CGF widget property, which should streamline the DER review.

items.title: Evaluate CGF vendor toolkit performance against current GPU budget

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Kicked off profiling of the vendor CGF toolkit's rendering pipeline against our current display processor's GPU frame budget, focusing on worst-case scenes with all attitude and bank widgets animating simultaneously.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Results show the CGF toolkit adds roughly 1.8ms per frame versus the legacy renderer under worst-case load, which still leaves comfortable headroom against our 16.6ms frame budget at 60Hz.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Recommendation is to proceed with the vendor toolkit as-is for this display generation; flagged a note for the next hardware refresh cycle that the headroom shrinks significantly if we add synthetic vision compositing on the same GPU.

comments.author: Meryl Streep
comments.text: This epic is the direct response to the line-check readability complaints — adaptive contrast, horizon line color compliance, anti-reflective outlining, and numeral wash-out under direct sun all roll up here.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Three of five items are through peer review; the horizon line color story is the one taking longer since it's gated on colorimetry data we don't fully control.

comments.author: Samuel L. Jackson
comments.text: The sun-table results on the adaptive contrast algorithm look strong. I want to make sure the horizon line color issue doesn't slip past this sprint since it's the one item our DER specifically called out.

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Four of five items resolved or live in prod. The horizon line color story remains blocked on the vendor's updated colorimetry reference sheet — we've asked for a firm delivery date and will reassess at next sprint planning.

items.title: Implement adaptive contrast algorithm for direct-sunlight conditions

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Reviewing the ambient light sensor data sheet against our contrast requirements — the sensor's dynamic range should be sufficient, but I want to confirm sample rate is fast enough to catch the transition when an aircraft banks into direct sun on approach.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: First pass of the adaptive contrast algorithm is running on the bench, scaling widget brightness and outline weight in response to the ambient sensor reading with a 200ms response time.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Reviewed the algorithm's transition curve — suggested smoothing the brightness ramp with a slight ease-out rather than linear scaling so it doesn't feel abrupt to the pilot, which is a quick change.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Deployed to production build after the saturation overshoot fix passed the full sun-table regression; pilot-in-the-loop feedback from the simulator session this week was positive on the smoothed transition curve.

subtasks.title: Characterize ambient light sensor input range for adaptive algorithm

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Characterized the sensor across its full 0 to 100,000 lux range and found a nonlinear response above 80,000 lux that needs to be accounted for in the algorithm's scaling function.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Published the full characterization curve to the shared requirements doc, including the nonlinear correction factor for the high end of the range.

storyBugs.title: Adaptive contrast algorithm overshoots at sensor saturation threshold

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: On the sun table at the maximum 100,000 lux setting, the widget brightness scaling overshoots to full intensity and then visibly clips back down about half a second later — distracting and not present at lower lux settings.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: The nonlinear correction factor above 80,000 lux wasn't being applied in the runtime scaling function, only in the offline characterization — added the correction to the live algorithm and the overshoot is gone in bench testing.

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: Re-tested across the full lux range including several passes at maximum saturation and the overshoot no longer occurs; closing this out.

items.title: Redesign horizon line color palette for glare compliance

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Pulled the current horizon line color values and cross-referenced them against the DO-160 Section 20 lighting environmental requirements — a few of our blue/brown shades sit right at the edge of the acceptable contrast ratio band.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Proposed a revised palette with wider contrast margins and submitted it for colorimetry validation, since any change here needs vendor sign-off on the physical display characteristics.

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: Pilot feedback from the sun-table session says the revised horizon color shift is still not clearly perceivable against the sky color at 50,000 lux, which doesn't meet the readability improvement we were targeting.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Reopened this one — the colorimetry data the vendor sent back doesn't match what we measured on the actual display panel, so I can't finalize a palette until they provide a corrected reference. Marking this blocked pending their updated data sheet.

subtasks.title: Run colorimetry validation against DO-160 Section 20 lighting profile

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Ran the initial colorimetry validation pass on the bench display against the DO-160 Section 20 profile; results are documented but flagged as needing vendor cross-check since our measurement rig isn't calibration-certified for this test.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Validation data package finalized and sent to the display vendor for their independent confirmation ahead of finalizing the palette.

storyBugs.title: Horizon line color shift not perceivable at 50,000 lux per pilot feedback

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: Two of three pilot evaluators in the sun-table session could not reliably distinguish the new horizon color from the old one at 50,000 lux, meaning the revised palette isn't delivering the intended readability gain.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Traced this to the vendor's colorimetry reference sheet using a different white-point calibration than our bench rig, so the palette I derived from it doesn't translate correctly onto the physical panel.

comments.author: Samuel L. Jackson
comments.text: Flagging this as a schedule risk — we need the vendor's corrected white-point data before this can move forward, and I'd like a firm commitment date from them by next week's sync.

items.title: Add anti-reflective symbology outline for high-glare cockpit glass

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Looking at adding a dark outline stroke around key symbology to improve contrast against reflections off the cockpit glass — the tricky part is keeping stroke width consistent across the two display vendors we support.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: First implementation renders a 1.5-pixel outline on all primary tape symbology; visually it's a clear improvement in the glare booth even without full sun-table testing yet.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Reviewed — outline rendering logic is solid, requested the stroke width be pulled into a shared constant rather than duplicated across the widget classes, which keeps it consistent if we tune it later.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Resolved after fixing the cross-vendor rendering inconsistency; both display vendors now render the outline within 0.1 pixel of each other in bench comparison.

subtasks.title: Prototype outline stroke width variants for readability testing

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Built three stroke width prototypes at 1, 1.5, and 2 pixels for the glare booth evaluation session next week.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Glare booth evaluators preferred the 1.5-pixel variant as the best balance of contrast improvement without looking heavy-handed; carrying that forward into the main implementation.

storyBugs.title: Outline stroke renders inconsistently across the two display vendors

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: Side-by-side comparison on both vendor display units shows the outline stroke rendering noticeably thinner on Vendor B's panel, roughly 1.1 pixels versus the intended 1.5, likely a sub-pixel rendering difference between the two graphics pipelines.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Confirmed Vendor B's CGF implementation rounds stroke width differently than Vendor A's — added an explicit anti-aliasing hint to the widget property that forces consistent rounding on both platforms.

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: Verified stroke width now matches within measurement tolerance on both vendor panels; closing this out.

items.title: Airspeed tape numerals wash out under simulated 85,000 lux sun table

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: At 85,000 lux on the sun table, the airspeed tape's numeral font weight is too thin to remain legible against the washed-out background — this is the same font weight used across all tape numerals, so it may affect altitude too.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Confirmed the issue is isolated to airspeed for now since its numerals sit on a lighter background panel than altitude; bumped the font weight and added the same dark outline treatment from the epic's anti-reflective work.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Updated rendering passed initial glare booth check; scheduling a full sun-table re-test to confirm at the original 85,000 lux failure condition.

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: Re-tested at 85,000 lux and the numerals remain clearly legible with the bolder weight and outline; also spot-checked altitude tape and confirmed it wasn't affected by the original issue.

items.title: Update glare-testing bench procedure for CDS software revision

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: The current glare-testing bench procedure references symbol IDs from the legacy renderer, which no longer apply after the widget migration, so I'm rewriting the procedure against the new CGF widget names.

comments.author: Charlize Theron
comments.text: Reviewed the draft procedure — looks complete, added a note to include the new adaptive contrast sensor calibration step at the top since testers will need to zero it before each session.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Procedure finalized and published to the QA test library, including the sensor calibration step and updated widget references throughout.

epics.title: Airspeed and Altitude Tape Rendering Modernization

comments.author: Meryl Streep
comments.text: This epic covers rebuilding both the airspeed and altitude tapes on the new widget pipeline, plus closing out two carryover bugs against the current baro correction and color band logic.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Airspeed tape rebuild hit a snag in testing this week with a trend vector lag issue that required a second look, but the fix is in and re-verification is scheduled.

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Good recovery on the trend vector lag — reopened once but resolved cleanly on the second pass. The AFM color band mismatch bug is still on hold pending updated limits from the performance engineering team.

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Four of five items resolved or live in prod this month; the color band bug stays on hold until performance engineering delivers the revised AFM limits, expected early next sprint.

items.title: Rebuild airspeed tape rendering pipeline using ARINC 661 vector widgets

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Mapping out the airspeed tape's moving scale, fixed reference line, and trend vector onto vector widgets — the trend vector is the most complex piece since it needs to recompute every frame off the ADIRU rate data.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Core tape and scale widgets are working on the bench; trend vector calculation is ported but I haven't stress-tested it under rapid acceleration yet.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Reviewed the trend vector math — logic looks correct against the spec, requested a comment explaining the smoothing filter constant since it's not obvious why that particular value was chosen.

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: During rapid acceleration testing on the HIL bench, the trend vector visibly lags the actual airspeed by up to 400 milliseconds, which is well outside the 100 millisecond spec and could mislead a pilot during a go-around.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Reopening to fix — the smoothing filter constant Viola flagged earlier was tuned for steady-state smoothness but wasn't validated against rapid transients, which is exactly what's causing the 400ms lag. Reducing the filter's time constant to correct this.

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: Re-tested the updated filter constant across five rapid-acceleration profiles including a simulated go-around, and trend vector lag is now consistently under 80 milliseconds. Resolving.

subtasks.title: Port airspeed trend vector calculation to new widget event model

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Ported the trend vector calculation from the legacy polling loop to the new widget event model, which fires on ADIRU data arrival instead of a fixed timer.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Updated the port to use the corrected smoothing filter constant from the story-level fix; event-driven update timing is confirmed working correctly.

storyBugs.title: Airspeed tape widget occasionally fails to initialize trend vector on cold start

comments.text: On roughly 1 in 20 cold starts of the CDS, the trend vector widget comes up blank until the first airspeed change event fires, rather than initializing to a zero-rate state immediately.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: Ran 50 cold-start cycles on the bench and the trend vector now initializes correctly to zero-rate every time; resolving.

items.title: Rebuild altitude tape with digital altitude window and VSI integration

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Scoping the altitude tape rebuild — in addition to the tape widget itself, this needs a digital altitude readout window and an integrated VSI needle, both of which are new compared to the legacy display.

comments.author: Viola Davis

comments.author: Viola Davis

subtasks.title: Define altitude alert banding thresholds in requirements traceability matrix

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Traceability matrix entries reviewed and signed off by the systems engineer; no discrepancies found against the certification basis document.

storyBugs.title: Altitude tape digit roller animation stutters near flight level transitions

comments.author: Natalie Portman
comments.text: During a rapid climb through FL180 on the HIL bench, the altitude digit roller visibly stutters for about two frames right at the ten-thousands digit rollover, which looks jarring compared to the smooth motion elsewhere in the climb.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Found it — the roller animation was recalculating its interpolation keyframes only when the leading digit changed, causing a visible hitch exactly at digit rollovers. Fixed by recalculating keyframes continuously instead.

comments.author: Natalie Portman
comments.text: Re-tested through multiple flight level transitions including FL100, FL180, and FL290 and the roller animation is now smooth throughout. Resolving.

items.title: Altitude tape fails to reflect baro correction after QNH entry

comments.author: Natalie Portman

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Confirmed the altitude tape widget only listens for ADIRU altitude updates, not baro correction events specifically, so it misses the QNH change until the next regular data refresh.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Added a dedicated event subscription for baro correction changes so the tape updates immediately on QNH entry rather than waiting for the next refresh cycle.

comments.author: Natalie Portman
comments.text: Verified the tape now updates within one frame of QNH entry across ten repeated test entries; closing this out.

items.title: Airspeed tape color band thresholds do not match updated AFM limits

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson
comments.text: Pulled the display config and confirmed the color band thresholds are hardcoded from the old AFM revision rather than reading from the shared performance limits table, which is the real underlying issue here.

comments.author: Scarlett Johansson

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Placing this on hold — performance engineering says the finalized AFM limits won't be delivered until early next sprint, so there's no point implementing against a value that could still shift.

items.title: Investigate feasibility of merging airspeed and altitude tape render loops into a single frame buffer

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Investigating whether merging the airspeed and altitude tape render loops into a shared frame buffer would meaningfully reduce GPU overhead, since right now they're rendered as two fully independent passes.

items.title: Color-code terrain by relative altitude bands per SVS color convention

items.title: Terrain rendering causes frame drop below 20 fps in mountainous approach profiles

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: During the simulated Queenstown-style approach, frame rate drops to as low as 17 fps once terrain mesh density spikes on the steep valley walls, which is below our 20 fps display-currency requirement.

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Root cause is uncapped mesh subdivision on steep slopes; added a dynamic subdivision cap tied to camera pitch angle so we trade a small amount of visual fidelity for guaranteed frame rate on extreme terrain.

comments.author: Idris Elba

items.title: Implement rate-of-change suppression for fluctuating fuel quantity alerts

items.title: Perform boresight registration verification against aircraft datum

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: This verification directly supports the conformality claim in our certification basis, so I want measurements taken across the full eyebox, not just the design eye reference point.

comments.text: Reviewed the measurement methodology and it matches the approach we validated on a prior program. One suggestion: capture ambient temperature during each measurement since combiner optics can shift slightly with thermal expansion.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Added temperature logging as suggested and completed the full nine-position campaign after resolving the tolerance issue at extreme eye positions below. This is now supporting flight test operations.

subtasks.title: Conduct optical bench registration measurement campaign

storyBugs.title: Registration error exceeds 2 mrad tolerance at extreme eye position

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: At the extreme lateral eyebox position, registration error measured 2.4 mrad against our 2.0 mrad certification tolerance. Every other position was comfortably within limits.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Traced it to a slight mechanical play in the combiner mount at that extreme angle. Applied a shim adjustment and re-measured, getting it down to 1.1 mrad.

comments.author: Idris Elba
comments.text: First re-verification pass looked good, but a second independent measurement the next day showed it had crept back up to 1.9 mrad, so I reopened this rather than sign off prematurely.

comments.author: Denzel Washington
comments.text: Found the shim had settled slightly under repeated thermal cycling. Replaced it with a locking variant and confirmed stable sub-1 mrad readings across five separate measurement sessions. Confident this one is truly closed now.

items.title: Assess feasibility of digital light engine vs CRT-based HUD projector

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Compared reliability and brightness specs between a digital light engine projector and our current CRT-based unit. The digital unit offers better brightness stability over its service life but has a shorter qualified flight history.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: Talked to two suppliers and the digital light engine option would require its own DO-160 environmental qualification campaign, which isn't feasible within this program's schedule. Recommending we stay on the CRT projector for this certification cycle.

comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Agreed with staying on the CRT projector given the schedule constraint, but let's capture the digital light engine option as a candidate for the next major avionics refresh. Closing the spike.

items.title: Prepare hardware-in-the-loop bench for final conformality regression suite

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Started reconfiguring the HIL bench to run the full conformality regression suite end to end rather than the individual test scripts we've been using. About halfway through the bench wiring changes.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Putting this on hold — the bench needs a replacement signal generator card that's backordered from the supplier until mid-August. Individual test scripts still work in the meantime, so this doesn't block other testing, just the consolidated regression run.

comments.text: This migration is the long-pole dependency for every future sensor-fusion initiative on the roadmap - ARINC 429's point-to-point bandwidth ceiling is already forcing us to ration data on the EICAS feed, and DO-178C recertification for the display network will need to accompany any architecture change here. I want a switch fabric topology locked before we commit engineering hours to the protocol bridge work.

comments.text: Fleet operations is watching this closely - three of the newer airframes are already bandwidth-constrained on the legacy 429 backbone, and any slip here pushes out the synthetic vision rollout that depends on the extra headroom. comments.author: Bill Blair
comments.text: Switch fabric and protocol bridge work are both resolved and moving to live traffic; the bandwidth allocation epic has one item on hold pending network qualification lab time, which I've escalated with facilities. items.title: Switch fabric drops frames under burst traffic from ADIRU sensor fusion feed

comments.text: Under the ADIRU burst traffic profile, the switch fabric is dropping roughly 2% of frames during peak load - reproducible consistently in the integration lab rig.

comments.author: Emma Stone

comments.author: Charlize Theron

comments.author: Emma Stone
comments.text: Ran the thermal soak variant of the burst test and the buffer fix holds steady with zero drops; marking resolved and adding the thermal case to the standard regression suite.

items.title: Add end-system health monitoring for protocol bridge redundancy management

comments.author: Emma Stone

comments.author: Emma Stone

storyBugs.title: Health monitor fails to detect a silent end-system failure within required 200ms window

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: The hard power-failure case triggers failover fine, but a silent failure - where the end-system stays powered but stops processing - isn't detected until nearly 400ms, well outside the requirement.

comments.author: Viola Davis
comments.text: The heartbeat frame was being generated by a lower-level NIC driver that kept running even when the application logic hung, masking the failure. Moved heartbeat generation into the application layer so it reflects true processing health.

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: Retested the silent-failure scenario with the application-layer heartbeat - detected and failed over in 95ms; resolved.

items.title: Protocol bridge introduces 40ms latency spike during dual-lane failover

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: During dual-lane failover testing on the protocol bridge, end-to-end latency spikes to about 90ms for roughly 40ms duration, pushing past the 50ms budget for flight-critical data during that window.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: The spike happens because the backup lane has to rebuild its routing table from scratch on failover instead of keeping a warm copy; that rebuild is what's eating the extra time.

comments.author: Leonardo DiCaprio
comments.text: Implemented a warm-standby routing table that syncs continuously from the primary lane, so failover just has to activate it instead of rebuilding; latency spike down to about 12ms in bench testing.

comments.author: Morgan Freeman
comments.text: Verified the warm-standby fix across twenty failover cycles, worst case latency spike was 14ms, comfortably under budget; resolved.
